newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Nedlloyd hits rough seas in 1996, profits dive.
newsitem.headline: Nedlloyd hits rough seas in 1996, profits dive.

text.p: Dutch shipping and road transport group Konkinlijke Nedlloyd Groep NV on Thursday announced a 54 percent slide in net profit after extraordinary items to 49 million guilders ($25.8 million) for calendar 1996.

Nedlloyd, which merged its container shipping operations with those of Peninsula and Oriental Steam Navigation Company last year, also said it was too early to make a forecast for its P&O Nedlloyd joint venture.
But it saw continuing pressure in rates in the current year.
The 1996 result was marred by the inclusion in the result for 1995 of net extraordinary gains of 29 million guilders. There were no such non-recurring items in 1996.

Before extraordinaries, the result from ordinary operations was 33 percent lower at 53 million guilders ($27.9 million), while operating profit fell 25 percent to 104 million guilders ($54.8 million).
The dividend of 1.25 guilders per share was unchanged.

Nedlloyd said operating profit from the Ocean Shipping division more than halved to 25 million guilders from 57 million in 1995 and, if capital gains on the sale of vessels was excluded, it dropped 48 million guilders.
It said ocean shipping results deteriorated in the first six months of 1996 but improved markedly in the second half.
The company said European Transport and Distribution results rose to 52 million guilders from 47 million.

"The fundamental improvement (especially in Germany) is even better, due to the representation of the operational results for Austria through the first three quarters of 1995 being too favourable," Nedlloyd said.
Results from the Nedrill unit, sold on July 1, 1996 to Noble Drilling Corp of the United States, and other activities fell to 27 million guilders from 34 million.
Nedlloyd also said it was considerably better equipped for the future following the P&O merger, which was on schedule.
"The merger's advantages will steadily become visible in the course of the year, but are not yet visible in the first quarter, traditionally a weak volume period," it said.
"Moreover, we expect continuing pressure on rates in 1997. It is therefore too early to project a concrete result for P&O Nedlloyd."
But Nedlloyd said it expected further improvement from all activities in European Transport and Distribution.
Martinair, the charter and freight group jointly owned with national carrier KLM, made a considerably lower contribution to the 1996 result due to pressure on fares and a rise in fuel costs.
But it was expected to show a better result in 1997, Nedlloyd added.
Analysts had forecast a net profit before extraordinaries of between 20 million and 38 million guilders.
